commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename Duke to MattChatBot, greet and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Rename the chatbot to MattChatBot and remove all traces of the placeholder
Duke name from the code and the docs, so the product has an identity of its
own rather than the template's.

Replace the banner-only main method with separate greet() and exit() steps.
Splitting them now leaves a clear seam where the command loop goes in
Level-1, instead of having to break apart a single long main later. The
banner uses a text block rather than concatenated "\n" strings, which keeps
the ASCII art readable and editable in the source.

Fill in the student profile in AGENTS.md and add command-line build/run
instructions to the README, since the project is being developed in VS Code
rather than IntelliJ.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-1: Echo user commands until bye
commitResults.messageBody:
Add an input loop between the greeting and the farewell, echoing each line
back to the user and stopping on the bye command.

Guard the loop with hasNextLine() rather than calling nextLine() in an
infinite loop, so that input ending without an explicit bye (Ctrl-D at the
keyboard, or piped input running out) exits cleanly instead of throwing
NoSuchElementException.

Extract a say() helper, since the greeting, the echo and the farewell all
wrap their output in the same dividers; this also gives later increments one
place to change the reply format.

Update the README sample output, which still showed the bot exiting
immediately rather than waiting for commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-2: Store and list user input
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the echo behaviour with simple command handling: the list command
prints everything stored so far, numbered from 1, and any other input is
stored and confirmed with "added: <text>".

Store items in a fixed String[100] with a separate count, as the requirements
allow and cap at 100 items. Guard the add path so that exceeding the cap
reports that the list is full rather than throwing
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and report an empty list explicitly rather
than printing a blank block. Blank input lines are ignored so they do not
become empty entries.

Rename echoUntilBye() to runCommandLoop(), as it no longer echoes, and update
the README sample output to show the new add/list behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Mark tasks as done, add Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Add mark and unmark commands so the user can set and reverse a task's done
status, and show that status in the list output, which now carries the
"Here are the tasks in your list:" header and a [X] or [ ] box per task.

Follow the A-Classes extension required by this increment: introduce a Task
class in its own file, holding the description together with its done state.
A plain String had nowhere to keep that state, so the stored items had to
become objects; Task also owns its own display format via toString(), which
keeps the rendering next to the data it describes.

Split input on the first space so that mark and unmark can be told apart from
task descriptions that merely start with those words. Reject a missing,
non-numeric or out-of-range task number with a message instead of throwing;
proper error handling arrives in Level-5.

Update the README sample output, and its compile command, which now needs to
cover both source files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Add todos, deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Add todo, deadline and event commands so the bot tracks the three task types
required by this increment. Deadlines take a /by and events take a /from and
a /to; dates stay as free text, as the requirements allow at this stage.

Follow the A-Inheritance extension required by this increment: Todo, Deadline
and Event now extend Task, rather than Task carrying a type field and a
branch for each type. Task becomes abstract with an abstract getTypeIcon(),
since nothing creates a typeless task any more and each subclass can supply
its own marker; Deadline and Event extend toString() via super, so the
"[T][X] description" prefix is defined in exactly one place.

Unrecognised input can no longer be stored verbatim, because a bare string
has no task type, so it now reports the available commands instead.
Malformed todo, deadline and event commands report the expected form rather
than storing a half-built task; Level-5 replaces these ad hoc checks with
proper error handling.

Update the README sample output to cover the three task types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Handle invalid input with exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow the A-Exceptions extension required by this increment: add a
MattChatBotException carrying a message written for the user, throw it from
the command methods, and catch it in one place in the command loop. The loop
reports the message and continues, so a bad command never ends the session.
Making it a checked exception means the compiler requires every command path
to either handle the problem or pass it up to that single reporting point.

Handle every error the current version can hit, not only the two shown in the
requirements: unknown commands, a todo with no description, a deadline or
event missing its /by, /from or /to or the text after them, a task number
that is missing, non-numeric or outside the list, and a full list.

Locate /by, /from and /to by position rather than splitting on " /by "
surrounded by spaces. The previous approach reported "needs a /by" for
"deadline /by Sunday" and for a trailing "/by" with nothing after it, since
neither has the surrounding spaces the split looked for; both messages named
the wrong problem. Searching for /to only after /from also stops a
description that mentions /to from being read as the end time.

Update the README with an example of an error reply.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-6: Delete tasks, store them in an ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a delete command that removes a task by its list number and reports what
was removed along with how many tasks remain.

Follow the A-Collections extension required by this increment: replace the
fixed Task[100] and its separate count with an ArrayList. The list now grows
as needed, so the 100-task ceiling and the "list is full" error are gone, and
removal closes the gap by itself rather than needing a shift loop. Task
numbers therefore renumber after a delete, which the requirements' example
relies on.

Reuse the existing task-number parsing for delete, so a missing, non-numeric
or out-of-range number is reported the same way as for mark and unmark.
Extract countSummary() and describeCount(), now that both add and delete
report the remaining count.

Update the README to cover the delete command.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: Represent commands as an enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the string literals driving command dispatch with a Command enum,
each constant holding the keyword the user types.

The keywords previously existed in two places: as literals in the dispatch
switch, and again inside the "I don't know what that means" message listing
them. Nothing kept the two in step, and adding delete in Level-6 required
remembering to update both. The message is now generated from the enum, so
the list cannot go stale.

Dispatch is now a switch expression over the enum rather than a switch
statement over strings. Since every branch yields the exit flag, the compiler
requires the switch to be exhaustive: adding a constant to Command fails the
build until it is handled, which a string switch with a default branch could
never catch. Messages that named a command now read the keyword from the enum
for the same reason.

Behaviour is unchanged, including case-insensitive command words.
